Timer part only: new `timerAnchor` state; setTimer re-anchors from each server frame and starts/stops a module-level phase-aligned setTimeout ticker that decrements `timer.time_remaining` locally at 1 Hz (never counts up, stops at 0); anchor cleared + ticker stopped in setTimer(null), runBattleAtomicReset and resetMatchState; visibilitychange->visible re-derives immediately.

NEW pure helpers: planDispatch (leading+trailing throttle with forceNow and minTrailingDelay), potSignatureOf (each side quantised to 0.5 % of total pot + 5 % log bucket on total), priceSideOf (verdict side of the price signature).
NEW spec for the throttle plan, pot quantisation (ignores sub-0.5 % churn, tracks real moves and ~5 % growth, stable on empty pots) and side extraction.

Rewritten fetch loop (audit E1): requestId per DISPATCH, leading+trailing 750 ms throttle, immediate dispatch on verdict-side change, pending trailing dispatch survives dependency changes (no cleanup-clear = no starvation), abort+invalidate on battle change / disable.

Same requestId-per-dispatch fix; <= 1 req/s leading+trailing throttle with a 200 ms minimum trailing delay for keystrokes; trailing dispatch reads latest battleId/amount from a ref updated in an effect.
potSignature now potSignatureOf(buyPot, sellPot) (0.5 % quantisation); VERDICT_DAMP_MS 1500 -> 300.

Pool bar (audit B1/P1): $ labels moved out of the clamped fills into the track as absolutely positioned children; a layout effect measures label widths (only when the formatted labels change) and widens --min-pos/--max-pos so the dot never covers digits; the smoothing rAF loop is started from the sellPercent effect and stops itself when converged, writes --sell-percent only when the value changed.

.progress-sell/.progress-buy become pure colour fills (padding/flex removed); new `.progress-bar-track > .progress-label` absolute rules (z-index 10 above the dot, pointer-events none, text-shadow), .progress-label-sell left:12px, .progress-label-buy right:12px.
startDroppedFrameMonitor is a no-op unless import.meta.env.DEV, window.__TT_FRAME_MONITOR__ === true, or {force:true} (audit P1/F5).

Match-slice persistence now goes through the 750 ms trailing throttle; `price`/`timer` removed from the trigger slice (price read at flush time, timer never persisted); flush immediately on visibilitychange->hidden and pagehide; skips persisting when not authenticated; writes `userId`; no candle mirror (C1).

Snapshot carries `userId`; resolveResumeUserId() (localStorage user record) and isResumeSnapshotForAnotherUser(); onRehydrateStorage ignores + clears a snapshot written for another user (audit F9); clearSnapshot resets to initialState.
logout() now calls appResumeStore.clearSnapshot() and clearSessionResumeState() after the existing resets.

New exported SESSION_RESUME_KEYS + clearSessionResumeState() (removes app-resume-snapshot, ticktrade-resume, ticktrade:sessionBattleId, tt_linechart_candleClosed_session_v1 from sessionStorage); clearStorageOnRedirectToLogin() calls it. Literal keys on purpose (imported by the axios interceptor — no store imports).

Stale watchdog (audit P3): 12 s threshold floor + 0-4 s jitter (resolveStaleThresholdMs), cheap `ping` ack probe (probeSocket, 2.5 s timeout) before reconnect; onAlive callback when the probe acks or data arrived meanwhile; document.hidden guard made SSR-safe; stop() flag prevents late callbacks.
NEW spec: threshold floor/jitter, probeSocket ack/timeout/fallback shapes, watchdog alive-vs-reconnect decisions, data-arrived-during-probe, healthy never probes.
lineChartStore selector returns the last close as a number (or null) instead of the candle object, so the badge re-renders only when the close changes (audit F10).

Workbox: CacheFirst for same-origin /assets/* (hashed, immutable), NetworkFirst kept for icons/sounds/manifest/woff2; precache list extended with the arena path (index/App/AppShell js+css, router, zustand, axios, socket, lightweight-charts, MainLayout, Matches, MatchesChatSection, NewChart, ChartData, Trading, WinEstimatorSheet, hooks, useBattleCountdown, useVisiblePots); `build.esbuildOptions` (ignored by Vite) moved to top-level `esbuild: { drop, pure }` so console.* is really stripped.

behaviour_changes: Battle countdown ticks locally at 1 Hz between server timerUpdate frames (anchored to the last frame; server frames re-anchor, snapping when they differ by >= 1 s). A late/dropped frame no longer freezes the digits; the local clock only counts DOWN and stops at 0; server 0 always wins.

Timer/price payloads are accepted while the client has no battle id (isActiveBattlePayload returns true for activeBattleId == null); useWebSocket must adopt battle_id from the tick (request to pwa-shell) for the T10 fix to be complete.
timerUpdate frames up to 2 s older than the last seen timestamp are accepted (clock skew between API host and engine host); other events keep strict ordering.

Market Flip: fetches at most every 750 ms (leading+trailing), fires immediately when the price crosses the round price, pot changes below 0.5 % of the total pot no longer retrigger, responses are only discarded when a newer request was actually sent, verdict damper 300 ms (was 1500).
Scenario estimate: <= 1 POST /battle/estimate-payout per second per open sheet (was up to 2-4/s); same requestId fix.

Pool bar: both $ labels are always fully visible (absolute children of the track above the dot); the fill clamp widens to the measured label width so the dot never sits on the digits (fallback 13 %/87 % unchanged). Smoothing rAF stops when converged instead of running at 60 fps for the whole round.
Dropped-frame telemetry rAF loop no longer runs in production (DEV or explicit opt-in only).

Resume snapshot is written at most every 750 ms (plus an immediate flush on hide/pagehide) instead of on every price tick; price/timer are no longer triggers; timer is never persisted; candles never persisted.
Resume snapshot is bound to the user id: cleared on logout and on every auth-redirect path (401, guest error, login page), and ignored+cleared on boot if it belongs to another account.

Stale-socket watchdog: threshold floor 12 s + 0-4 s jitter (call-site values below the floor are raised), and a cheap `ping` ack probe runs before any forced reconnect; a socket that answers is left alone (onAlive). Until the backend adds the `ping` handler the probe times out after 2.5 s and the old reconnect happens (later and jittered).
PriceBadge re-renders only when the last chart close changes.

Service worker: hashed /assets/* served CacheFirst, arena chunks precached (38 entries, ~1.2 MB); console.log/warn/info/debug are stripped from production bundles (verified: 0 occurrences of the previously leaked warn string in dist).
new_settings_env: window.__TT_FRAME_MONITOR__ = true (browser console, runtime-only debug switch): enables the dropped-frame rAF monitor in production builds; default off. No new build-time env vars.

notes_for_pdf:
Scope of this change set: the trading-panel countdown, the pool bar, the Profit Estimator fetch loops, several always-on client loops, the per-tab resume snapshot, the stale-socket watchdog and the PWA build/service-worker configuration. All files are under /home/claude/wb/frontend.

1. Countdown freezes (audit T1, T9, T10 — contract C2). The digits were a verbatim copy of the last `timerUpdate` frame; any late, dropped or throttled frame froze them and the catch-up burst afterwards made them jump. `src/stores/matchStore.js` now keeps a `timerAnchor` (`remaining`, `receivedAt`, `battleId`) for the last server frame and a phase-aligned 1 Hz `setTimeout` ticker (pure logic in `src/live/utils/timerCountdownAnchor.js`) decrements `timer.time_remaining` locally between frames, recomputing `time_elapsed`/`percentage_complete` when `total_duration` is known. Every server frame re-anchors: if it differs from the local clock by >= 1 s the anchor snaps to the server (reconnect, resume, drift); otherwise the local phase is kept so the digits do not jitter. Safety properties relevant to trading: the local clock never counts up, stops at 0, and a server frame saying 0 always wins — so the client's trade gate can only close earlier than the server, never later. The ticker is stopped in `setTimer(null)`, `runBattleAtomicReset` and `resetMatchState`, and re-derives immediately on `visibilitychange` (background timer throttling). Consumers (`useBattleCountdown`, TradingPanel, IndicatorsPanel, NewChart) are unchanged because they still read `matchStore.timer`. `src/live/utils/realtimeEventGuards.js` additionally tolerates `timerUpdate` timestamps up to 2 s older than the last one (API host vs engine host clock skew) and `isActiveBattlePayload` accepts frames while the client has no battle id; the matching battle-id adoption inside `useWebSocket.js` is listed for the wave-2 shell agent.

2. Market Flip / estimator (E1, E3). `useMarketFlip` and `useWinEstimate` bumped their `requestId` on every effect run and restarted a trailing debounce on every dependency change, so under continuous NPC pool ticks they either sent nothing or discarded every response. Both now use a leading+trailing throttle (`src/live/utils/requestThrottle.js`: 750 ms for Market Flip, 1 s with a 200 ms keystroke debounce for the scenario cards), a `requestId` that increments per dispatched request only, and a trailing timer that deliberately survives dependency changes. A change of verdict side (price crossing the round price) fires immediately. `WinEstimatorSheet` quantises the pool signature to 0.5 % of the total pot (plus a 5 % bucket on the total) and the verdict damper drops from 1500 ms to 300 ms. Net effect: the LOSING row appears within roughly one round-trip of the crossing and refreshes at a bounded rate. No money math changed: both hooks still render exactly what the server returns.

3. Pool bar (B1, P1). The `$` labels were children of the width-clamped fills, so the small side's number was clipped and covered by the white dot. In `TradingPanel.jsx`/`TradingPanel.css` the labels are absolutely positioned children of `.progress-bar-track` (z-index above the dot, pointer-events none, text shadow); a layout effect measures the label widths only when the formatted amounts change and widens `--min-pos`/`--max-pos` (`max(13%, <label+dot>px)` / `min(87%, calc(100% - …))`) so the dot can never sit on the digits. The fills keep their clamp. The smoothing rAF loop now starts from the `sellPercent` effect and stops itself when converged, writing `--sell-percent` only when the value changed, instead of running at 60 fps for the whole round.

4. Client loops and re-renders (P1, P2/F3, F9, F10). `realtimeTelemetry.startDroppedFrameMonitor` is a no-op in production (DEV, `window.__TT_FRAME_MONITOR__ = true`, or `{force:true}`). `ResumeSyncBridge` now really uses its 750 ms throttle, no longer triggers on price/timer (price is read at flush time, timer is never persisted), flushes immediately on hide/pagehide, skips writes when logged out, and never persists candles (contract C1). `appResumeStore` stores the `userId`, ignores and clears a snapshot written by another account on boot, and is cleared by `authStore.logout()`; `clearStorageOnRedirectToLogin()` (401 interceptor, ProtectedRoute, Login, guest error) also removes the session keys (`clearSessionResumeState`). `PriceBadge` selects the last close as a number.

5. Stale watchdog (P3). `socketHealthService` enforces a 12 s stale floor plus 0–4 s per-client jitter and, before a forced reconnect, emits a `ping` with an ack (2.5 s timeout); a socket that answers, or that received data meanwhile, is reported via `onAlive` instead of being reconnected. The backend `ping` handler is requested from the api-core agent; until then the probe times out and the old reconnect happens, later and spread out.

6. PWA build (F8). `vite.config.js`: hashed `/assets/*` are served CacheFirst (they are immutable), the arena chunks (App, Matches, MainLayout, NewChart, lightweight-charts, socket, zustand, router, axios, Trading, WinEstimatorSheet, …) are precached, and the mis-nested `build.esbuildOptions` moved to top-level `esbuild` so `console.log/warn/info/debug` are really stripped (verified in dist).

How to test: `cd /home/claude/wb/frontend && node --test \"src/**/*.test.js\"` (63 tests: timer anchor, event guards, throttle/pot signature, watchdog) and `npx vite build`. Manually: with the new backend, watch the countdown keep ticking while the API is paused for a few seconds and snap back when frames resume; open the Profit Estimator during an NPC-heavy round and confirm the network tab shows <= ~1.3 market-flip and <= 1 estimate request per second and LOSING appears promptly after a crossing; make one pool tiny and confirm both `$` labels are readable with the dot clear of them; log out and back in as another user in the same tab and confirm no stale price/trades paint; in DevTools > Application > Service Workers confirm `ticktrade-assets` is CacheFirst.
